summary: Private deployment: DNS resolution failures + TLS handshake errors after upgrade to Redwood Private 2.14.0
description:
Issue Summary
- Customer reports that immediately after upgrading Redwood Private (control plane + private gateway bundle) from 2.13.2 -> 2.14.0, their application cannot reach Redwood endpoints in the private deployment.
- Symptoms alternate between:
  1) DNS resolution failures for internal Redwood hostnames (NXDOMAIN / SERVFAIL)
  2) TLS handshake failures when DNS does resolve (x509 / unknown authority / handshake alert)

Customer Impact
- ~65–80% of requests to /v1/chat.completions and /v1/embeddings fail from the customer’s application subnets.
- Partial recovery observed when customer routes traffic through a different subnet / DNS forwarder.
- Dedicated customer-facing product endpoints impacted; customer reports degraded chatbot feature for internal employees.

Environment
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC, AWS us-east)
- Upgrade window: 2025-11-18 16:40Z–17:05Z
- Connectivity path: app subnets -> internal DNS -> private ALB/NLB -> Redwood Private Gateway -> serving fleet
- Customer noted they use a split-horizon DNS setup with conditional forwarders for *.redwood.internal

Timeline (UTC)
- 2025-11-18 17:12Z: Customer opens Sev1 via Support hotline; initial report: “can’t resolve gateway hostnames; occasional TLS errors.”
- 2025-11-18 17:22Z: Support requests samples (dig/nslookup output, curl -v, gateway logs).
- 2025-11-18 17:45Z: SRE on-call pulled into #incidents (private) due to high failure rate; incident created (INC-2025-11-18-priv-conn-helios).
- 2025-11-18 18:15Z: Confirmed DNS failures correlate to a specific customer DNS resolver/forwarder pair.
- 2025-11-18 19:05Z: Confirmed TLS failures correlate to clients missing updated intermediate CA chain used by 2.14.0 gateway cert bundle.
- 2025-11-18 20:10Z: Workaround deployed by customer (update trust store + pin resolver); error rate drops <1%.
- 2025-11-19 00:30Z: Monitoring stable; incident resolved.
- 2025-11-25: Ticket closed after customer confirms no recurrence and completes follow-up validation.

Steps to Reproduce (from customer)
1) From app host in subnet A:
   - dig gateway.redwood.internal A @<resolver-ip> => intermittently SERVFAIL
   - curl -v https://gateway.redwood.internal/healthz => sometimes: "Could not resolve host"; other times: "SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate"
2) From app host in subnet B:
   - dig consistently returns A record
   - curl reaches /healthz but TLS fails on older AMI hosts only

Evidence / Logs (sanitized)
- DNS (intermittent):
  - ";; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL" (resolver <10.x.x.x>)
  - Occasional NXDOMAIN for gateway.redwood.internal
- TLS (clients on older base image):
  - "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority"
  - "SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed"
- Gateway logs around upgrade window show successful cert reload and no internal errors; no elevated 5xx at gateway once requests arrive.

Investigation Notes
- We validated this is not a serving runtime regression: once traffic reaches the gateway, request success rates are normal and p95 latency is unchanged.
- DNS side:
  - Customer’s conditional forwarder for *.redwood.internal points to two internal resolvers. One resolver began returning SERVFAIL after the upgrade.
  - The upgrade introduced an additional internal hostname for health checks (gateway now performs an internal self-check using a new name). This increased query volume to the conditional forwarders and exposed an existing resolver capacity/config issue (SERVFAIL under modest burst).
  - Customer resolver logs (shared on call) show rate-limiting and a misconfigured recursion/forwarding rule for the new hostname pattern.
- TLS side:
  - Redwood Private 2.14.0 gateway cert bundle moved to a new intermediate chain (no change to leaf CN/SANs, but different intermediate). Several customer app hosts did not have the updated intermediate CA in their trust store.
  - Affected hosts were running an older OS image; newer image hosts validated fine.

Classification (for Reliability Program / taxonomy validation)
- Proposed incident_type: Private Deployment Connectivity
- Proposed subtype: DNS resolution / TLS handshake
- Primary owner (recommended): Private Deployments
- Consulted: Infra/Networking (for DNS guidance), Security Ops (for cert chain/trust-store guidance)
- Notes: While the proximate trigger was the upgrade, the contributing factor was customer DNS forwarder config and client trust-store drift. We still track as reliability incident due to upgrade coupling + missing preflight validation.

Mitigation / Resolution
- Immediate mitigations applied:
  1) Customer pinned *.redwood.internal conditional forwarding to the healthy resolver while they adjusted the failing resolver configuration.
  2) Customer updated application host trust stores to include the new intermediate CA chain used by the 2.14.0 gateway cert bundle.
- Redwood actions:
  - Provided customer with the full CA chain file and verification steps.
  - Shared a recommended DNS preflight checklist for Private upgrades (query patterns + expected responses + suggested query rate headroom).

Customer Communication
- We confirmed no data integrity issues; this was connectivity only.
- We avoided asserting “root cause is customer misconfiguration” in writing; phrased as “upgrade introduced new certificate chain + additional internal DNS query pattern; existing resolver + trust-store posture was incompatible.”

Follow-ups
- Support/CS:
  - Add this incident to the Private upgrade readiness checklist for enterprise/private customers.
- Engineering (requested):
  - Add a preflight check in Private upgrade tooling to validate:
    - internal DNS can resolve all required hostnames from app subnets
    - client trust-store compatibility (or at least detect older base images and warn)
  - Document cert chain changes prominently in release notes and customer upgrade guide.

Next Update / Closure Criteria
- Close when customer confirms: (a) DNS stable across all resolvers, (b) TLS verification passes across all app hosts, (c) no recurrence for 5 business days.

Attachments
- Customer-provided: dig/nslookup output, curl -v output (sanitized)
- Redwood-provided: CA chain bundle + validation steps
